newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's consumer defaults up so far in November.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's consumer defaults up so far in November.

text.p: Consumer defaults in Sao Paulo city rose 19.6 percent to 91,175 in the first 15 days of November when compared with the same period of 1995, said the Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP).

It is early to say whether early November's higher consumer defaults, which are measured by the number of reported payments in arrears for over 30 days, indicate an uptrend but the figure has turned on the yellow light on the risk of another surge in consumer defaults, said Emilio Alfieri, economist at ASCP.
"It is a warning signal because consumers defaults are generally lower at year's end," Alfieri said, referring to the thirteenth salary paid to workers at this time of the year.
Alfieri said consumers defaults had declined between May and September and resumed rising in October, when defaults totalled 181,116, an increase of 18 percent compared with September.
He also said credit sales also slowed in the period, which may indicate retailer caution ahead of a possible rise in consumer defaults.
Odair Abate, economist at Lloyds Bank Brazil unit, also said it is too early to say how consumer insolvencies will develop, but he said he was surprised by the figures.
